3K.3 We should exercise compassion and pity towards the afflicted.
3K.9 To him that is afflicted, pity should be shown from his friend.

points: Job answers, wishing his grief were thoroughly weighed and his calamity laid in the balances; it would be heavier than the sand of the sea, so his words are swallowed up.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: The arrows of the Almighty are within him, their poison drinking up his spirit, and the terrors of God set themselves in array against him. He feels the full weight of the Most High's hand.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass, or the ox low over his fodder? A satisfied creature does not cry out; Job cries because he truly suffers.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Can that which is unsavory be eaten without salt, or is there taste in the white of an egg? The things his soul refused to touch have become his sorrowful meat.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Job longs that the Most High would grant his request and destroy him, letting loose His hand to cut him off. He would find comfort in that.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: He would harden himself in sorrow and not spare, for he has not concealed the words of the Holy One. Even wishing for death, Job holds fast to God's word.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: What is his strength that he should hope, and what is his end that he should prolong his life? His strength is not the strength of stones, nor his flesh of brass.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: His help is not in himself, and wisdom is driven quite from him. He confesses he has no resource left in his own power.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: To the afflicted, pity should be shown from his friend, but the one who withholds it forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Job's brethren dealt deceitfully as a brook, as streams that pass away, blackish with ice and hidden snow, that vanish when they wax warm and are consumed out of their place when it is hot. His friends failed him when he needed them most.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing and perish. The troops of Tema and companies of Sheba looked and waited, and were confounded and ashamed because they had hoped.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Now Job's friends are nothing; they see his casting down and are afraid. He never asked them to bring a reward, deliver him from the enemy's hand, or redeem him from the mighty. He asked nothing of their substance.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue; cause me to understand wherein I have erred. Job asks to be shown his fault so he can understand the errors he has made and learn the lesson of his affliction.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: How forcible are right words, but what does your arguing reprove? Job asks how their anger fixes anything. He does not know what he did, so their reproof only feels like wind.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Job asks them to look upon him, for it would be evident if he lied. Return, he says, let it not be iniquity; his righteousness is in it.

note.label: Job 6: Job Pleads for His Cause to Be Weighed

points: Is there iniquity in his tongue? Cannot his taste discern perverse things? He invites them to judge him from head to toe to see if he is in sin, just as David asked God to search him.
